plan_review.notes: Reviewed the plan to dispatch merge-train.yml from the merge-train-validate.yml publish job using the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN instead of the coordinator-requested App token. Reviewer confirmed the deviation is justified by existing repo evidence (buildDispatchBindings / reconcile-lib.mjs, PR #1144), confirmed the GITHUB_TOKEN workflow_dispatch recursion exception applies, confirmed queue:max concurrency is safe against duplicate triggers, and asked for (1) a documented caveat that if: always() does not guarantee dispatch after a hard manual job cancellation (only after cancelled/failure/skipped verify results), and (2) a live post-merge acceptance check. Both incorporated: caveat documented in the handoff, live check to be performed post-merge. No alternative dispatch design was proposed (convergent).

rounds.notes: Reviewed the diff (merge-train-validate.yml + merge-train-validate-publish.test.ts). Confirmed YAML correctness (actions: write scoped to publish job only, step ordering, if: always() placement), confirmed github.rest.actions.createWorkflowDispatch is the correct Octokit REST method mapping to POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches, confirmed context.payload.repository.default_branch is a reliable field already relied on elsewhere in this repo (ci-recovery.yml, merge-train.yml, auto-rebase-prs.yml), confirmed actions:write on GITHUB_TOKEN is low-risk since this workflow only triggers via workflow_dispatch (no fork/PR triggers), and confirmed the new tests execute the real script against a stubbed dispatch call so they would fail against a broken/reverted implementation. No significant issues found.

Reviewed the second wake-up added in the same PR: merge-train.yml's `workflow_run` trigger now also lists 'CI' (branches: [main]), and the reconcile job's `if:` gains a storm guard requiring `workflow_run.event == 'push'` when `workflow_run.name == 'CI'`, mirroring the already-shipped deploy.yml pattern. Reviewer confirmed: no && / || precedence ambiguity (each clause independently parenthesized); CI's own triggers (push/schedule/pull_request, no workflow_dispatch) mean workflow_run.event for CI can only be push/schedule/pull_request, so the push-only guard correctly excludes PR-CI and hourly-schedule-CI completions while allowing push-to-main CI completions; Merge Train Validation's wake-up is left completely unrestricted (workflow_run.name != 'CI' clause) since Validation is only ever workflow_dispatch'd against ref=main; deliberately does NOT check workflow_run.conclusion (unlike deploy.yml) because reconcile must wake and re-evaluate on any CI completion (success/failure/cancelled) to preserve fail-closed semantics; pre-existing concurrency: { group: crawler-merge-train, queue: max } coalesces bursts safely since reconcile.mjs re-derives state from GitHub each run. New test file tests/unit/merge-train-workflow-triggers.test.ts (10 tests) parses the real YAML and re-transcribes+truth-tables the gate logic. No significant issues found.

rounds.notes: Reviewed two additions made in response to automated copilot-pull-request-reviewer threads on PR #1166: (A) the bot-authored 'Recover failed check publication' step in merge-train-validate.yml (force-completes a stale in_progress merge-train-candidate check as cancelled via checks.create with the same external_id/fingerprint when the main publish step's own checks.create fails after a successful app-token step), and (B) my own schedule/MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED carve-out added to merge-train.yml's reconcile job `if:` (mirroring the identical precedent in ci-recovery-incidents.yml lines 38-42) to also wake reconcile on a same-SHA scheduled CI completion, closing a gap where reconcile.mjs's mainHealthReason() picks whichever run (push or schedule) is newest by created_at as authoritative -- so a later in-progress schedule run could leave reconcile permanently un-woken without this carve-out. Reviewer independently traced state.mjs's latestChecksByName/trainCheckState (selects by highest check-run id, not created_at, among checks matching name+external_id+trustedAppId) and confirmed the recovery step's new checks.create call with the same fingerprint necessarily gets a higher id than the original in_progress check and therefore correctly shadows it (trainCheckState returns 'missing' as intended); confirmed `if: failure() && steps.app-token.outcome == 'success'` is exhaustive for its intended failure mode and does not race the subsequent `if: always()` Dispatch Merge Train step (independent GITHUB_TOKEN, unconditional); confirmed reusing the same App token is required and correct for the trustedAppId filter to match; confirmed vars.MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED is readable in job-level if: expressions per the working ci-recovery-incidents.yml precedent; confirmed the carve-out does not reintroduce a storm risk since reconcile.mjs re-derives state from GitHub on every wake and a 'nothing to do' wake for an unrelated SHA is a cheap no-op; confirmed the 2 new/updated tests in merge-train-workflow-triggers.test.ts (now 12 total) exactly match the updated if: string and cover both the enabled and still-blocked-for-PR cases. No significant issues found.
